title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (cote 136, the 1976 IHÉS talk on the divided-power de Rham complex). The surrounding pages build, for a PD-base (S, S^+, t), with S^+ a PD-ideal and t ∈ S^+, an auxiliary graded-commutative PD-algebra A_S. It has a PD-variable X_0 and odd/exterior generators, and carries two structures: a filtration Fil^• (a PD-adic/Hodge-type filtration in X_0) and a filtration by exterior degree. The page studies functoriality in the base, i.e. what happens under a morphism φ : (S, S^+, t) → (S', S'^+, t').

Morphisms φ_* : A_S → A_{S'} compatible with PD-structures are described by a couple (φ_0, A'_1). Here φ_0 : S → S' is the map on bases, and A'_1 (together with auxiliary coefficients B'_i) gives the image of the generators. Three conditions are imposed:
- condition 1) is not visible on this page;
- condition 2) relates A'_1 to φ_0(t);
- condition 3) is a 2-torsion condition, typical of divided powers of odd-degree elements, since x^2 = 2x^{[2]}.

Corollary 3. φ_* respects Fil iff A'_1 ∈ Fil^1 and B'_i ∈ Fil^{i-1} for i ≥ 1. Concretely this means A'_1 = a'_1 X_0 and B'_i = Σ_{j<i} b'_{ij} X_0^{j}. The conditions then become:
- (2′) a'_1 t' = φ_0(t);
- (3′) 2 b'_{ij} t' = 0.

φ_* respects the associated gradings iff A'_1 = a'_1 X_0 and all B'_i = 0. If moreover S^+ = (t)_{pd}, these morphisms correspond exactly to couples (φ_0, λ = a'_1), each extended canonically to A_S → A_{S'}.

Corollary 4. φ_* always respects the 'discriminant' filtration by exterior degree.

Worked example. Take S = k{T} (PD-polynomial algebra), S^+ = (T)_{pd}, t = T, and similarly S' = k'{T}. A PD-morphism φ_0 is then determined by φ_00 : k → k'{T}, written φ_00(λ) = Σ_{i≥0} δ_i(λ) T^{[i]}. Here δ_0 : k → k' is a ring map, making k' a k-extension, and the δ_i are 'differential operators'. They satisfy δ_i(1) = 0 for i ≥ 1 and a Leibniz rule. In the divided-power basis this rule must carry binomial coefficients: δ_i(λλ') = Σ_{j+k=i} C(i,j) δ_j(λ) δ_k(λ'). In other words, a ring homomorphism into the PD-power-series/polynomial algebra is a Hasse–Schmidt-type higher derivation written in the divided-power basis. The page breaks off there.

Purpose: understanding the base-change/functoriality of the PD de Rham (crystalline-type) construction, and its compatibility with the Hodge and exterior-degree filtrations.
errors: If the multiplicativity formula is read literally as δ_i(λλ') = Σ_{j+k=i} δ_j(λ)δ_k(λ') (as in the machine transcription), it is wrong in the divided-power basis: T^{[j]}T^{[k]} = C(j+k,j) T^{[j+k]}, so binomial coefficients are needed. The manuscript seems to contain a coefficient symbol c_{j,k} before δ_j, which would make it correct.
'B'_i = 0, i ≥ 0' should presumably read i ≥ 1, since the B'_i are indexed from 1.
Condition 1) is not restated on this page, so the full characterization cannot be checked here.

ideas.what: Description of morphisms of the auxiliary PD-algebra A_S over a change of PD-base by data (φ_0, A'_1, B'_i), with criteria for respecting the filtration and the grading
ideas.modern_name: base-change functoriality of PD-envelopes / divided-power de Rham complexes; filtered PD-morphisms

ideas.what: Ring maps k → k'{T} into a PD-polynomial ring as sequences δ_i of higher differential operators
ideas.modern_name: Hasse–Schmidt (iterative) higher derivations in the divided-power basis
ideas.where_published: EGA IV §16 treats differential operators and principal parts, related but not identical

ideas.what: Filtration by exterior degree ('filtration discriminante') always preserved
ideas.modern_name: stupid/exterior-degree filtration on a graded-commutative PD dga

deep.surprise_reason: Routine bookkeeping of the functoriality of a PD-algebra construction under base change, plus a standard description of PD-morphisms out of a field via higher derivations. Nothing here appears absent from the crystalline literature.
transcription_corrections: In the display A'_1 = a'_1 X_0 there is a λ written under a'_1 (i.e. a'_1 = λ), which explains the later 'couples (φ_0, λ)'.
Last line: the sum appears to include a coefficient (c_{j,k}, likely a binomial) before δ_j(λ)δ_k(λ'); it is not a plain Σ δ_jδ_k.
Line S' = k'{T}: the manuscript reads S'^+ = (T')_{pd}, t' = T (sic; presumably T').
'(crains guère)' is an uncertain reading of a marginal note.
'A_{*S*} → A_{S'} !' should probably read A_S → A_{S'}, the canonical extension under φ_*.
